## refactor(prt): introduce exchange particle registry package

````
Add an "exchange PRP" package subtype, which each PRT model can use internally to hold particles transferred in from coupled models. Currently, particles are owned by PRP packages, not by models. The idea here is to set up for particle exchanges without departing from the pattern of particle ownership by PRPs.

Playing off the existing acronym I figure we could say this is a "Particle Registry Package". The normal Particle Release Package is also a registry, too, this one is *just* a registry.

This is a "headless" package in that it sources/reads no input and is internal, not user-facing. Several package lifecycle hooks are overridden as no-ops. The exchange PRP does not contribute to the budget as particles in it are active and accounted for by the storage term. The PRP term is the release-time source of mass which moves PRP -> STORAGE -> TERMINATION.

This is a clean refactor/preparatory step for PRT exchanges. After this an exchange PRP will exist for each PRT model but it will have no effect until exchanges are implemented.
````

## fix(prt): distinguish cell exit from subcell exit events

````
We currently define the PRT OC package's `TRACK_EXIT` keyword option as enabling reporting when particles exit any grid feature (model, cell or subcell), and report all such events with event code (i.e. reason code) 1. Thus subcell exits in the ternary method appear identical in output to cell transitions, despite the fact that subcells are an implementation detail of the ternary method and occur in the interior of user-defined grid cells.

Distinguish subcell exit events from cell exits. Introduce a new PRT OC option `TRACK_SUBFEATURE_EXIT` which applies to all grid features below the level of the user-defined discretization (currently only subcell exits in DISV grids, but this could apply later to e.g. subreaches in surface water models, etc). The old `TRACK_EXIT` option now only applies to grid-scale features and above, i.e. cells (and models once we implement particle exchanges).

While this changes the results reported by PRT under the default settings (see changed test snapshots for instance &mdash; fewer path points, now only on cell faces, which nicely matches mp7 when ternary is forced on a structured grid) we think that since subgrid features are not likely to be of interest to most users, this is reasonable to consider a fix, not a breaking change.

This PR also moves exit event firing routines to their respective method types, following on #2433.

#### Rejected alternatives

We aborted/punted some alternative ideas to resolve this:

<details>
<summary><h5>Feature-specific event codes and OC options</h5></summary>
Introduce a new particle event code 6 for subcell exits, and new PRT OC options `TRACK_CELLEXIT` and `TRACK_SUBCELLEXIT` toggling reporting for the respective events. `TRACK_EXIT` remains and continues to work as defined, enabling exit reporting for all features, but becomes disabled default. Counterargument: proliferating reason codes and OC options like this (i.e., one for each specific sub-grid-scale feature type, for all possible grid types) seems not ideal.
</details>

<details>
<summary><h5>New output column for domain level</h5></summary>
Consider introducing a new output column indicating the domain level at which a feature exit event occurs: model = 1, cell (or equivalent e.g. reach) = 2, subgrid features = 3. This would allow keeping the same reason code for all exit events while giving the ability to distinguish them. Counterargument: pretty big change, think about it some more.
</details>
````
